title.narrative: REPAM Strengthening democracy and sovereignty of the Brazilian Amazon

description.narrative: The REPAM Brazil project aims to support vulnerable Amazonian communities in their struggle against socio-environmental degradation. REPAM-Brazil's 2023-2026 plan prioritizes: 1. Advocating for rights and dignity; 2. Fostering intercultural dialogues within the Catholic Church in the Amazon; 3. Promoting socio-environmental justice, good-living, and our common home; 4. Building networks, alliances, and synodality. REPAM is a church-based organization, working with grassroots organizations, Dioceses, Prelature, and social pastoral agents across the Brazilian Amazon, focusing on women and young people. The project directly benefits1,585 people (505 women, 280 men, and 200 families ). Key outcomes include strengthening socio-environmental agendas and celebrating REPAM Brazil's 10th anniversary with increased visibility at COP30. Outcome indicators involve training 150 community leaders in human rights, nature rights, intercultural dialogue, active listening, and public policies. Additionally, the project empowers 150 Amazonian women through workshops and networking to defend human rights, and initiatives addressing violence and other vulnerabilities impacting women. The third outcome centers on exchanging successful agroecological, solidarity economy, and good living (Bem Viver) projects among REPAM's supported groups. This involves sharing successful experiences in the Amazon region, sensitizing community leaders and 12 groups about food security, food sovereignty, agroecology, and gender. Main project activities encompass long-distance training, online and face-to-face workshops, exchanges, seminars, and the production of communication materials such as booklets and videos. The project aims to foster coordination and mobilization among women, and grassroots leaders in the region to defend rights, propose public policies, demand implementation from duty bearers, and strenghthening living well practises safeguarding the region's socio-biodiversity.
